feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: 25 years after 9/11, a reporter digs through the WNYC recordings from that day
entry.summary: Each year, fewer Americans remember 9/11. The radio archives of WNYC take us to Ground Zero as the planes hit.

entry.title: Investigators release information from flight data recorder in Miami plane crash
entry.summary: Safety investigators are releasing new details about the moments before the deadly cargo plane crash in Miami on Sunday, raising questions about the actions of the two pilots.

entry.title: A huge 11th-century tapestry of the Norman Conquest has (carefully) traveled to Engla
entry.summary: Part war propaganda, part comic strip, the 230-foot Bayeux Tapestry is back in England for the first time in 900 years. It depicts the 1066 Battle of Hastings, which ended Anglo-Saxon rule.

entry.title: After a bicycle crash, some motorcyclists stopped to help
entry.summary: A photojournalist was stuck, injured and without cell service, after he crashed into a boulder on his bicycle in Scotland. Three motorcyclists stopped to help.

entry.title: How television and literature wrestled with 9/11
entry.summary: Over the past 25 years, books and television series have reflected the events and fallout from 9/11 in both direct and indirect ways.

entry.title: It's been 23 years since an American man last won the U.S. Open. That may change soon
entry.summary: An American man is guaranteed to make the final of the U.S. Open after Ben Shelton's win over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarterfinals. Shelton faces American Frances Tiafoe next.

entry.title: Comedian Stavros Halkias talks new Netflix special, politics and the manosphere
entry.summary: Comedian and actor Stavros Halkias speaks with NPR's Juana Summers about his new stand up comedy special, Uncle Stav.

entry.title: Retired WNBA legend Tina Charles shares who to watch in FIBA World Cup
entry.summary: The FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup is underway in Germany. NPR's Scott Detrow and retired WNBA legend Tina Charles break down the brackets.

entry.title: Anthropic researcher resigns amid AI safety concerns
entry.summary: A researcher at the AI company Anthropic resigned with a warning that the entire artificial intelligence industry is designing tools that humans will soon lose control of.

entry.title: Are we any closer to detecting dark matter?
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with theoretical astrophysicist Priyamvada Natarajan of Yale University about a strange blip recorded by a dark matter detector in South Dakota and what the fluke could mean.
